paper_metadata.title: Effect of Nb addition in novel amorphous/nanocrystalline Ti-Zr-Cu-Ni-Nb brazing fillers on improving microstructure and mechanical properties of TiAl alloy joints

evidence.quote: Effect of Nb addition in novel amorphous/nanocrystalline Ti-Zr-Cu-Ni-Nb brazing fillers on improving microstructure and mechanical properties of TiAl alloy joints
TiAl alloys are promising light-weight high-temperature structural materials due to their high specific strength, low density, and good creep and oxidation resistance
Amorphous/nanocrystalline Ti-Zr-Cu-Ni(-Nb) alloy ribbons were synthesized and used as novel BFMs for brazing TiAl alloy.

Due to the improved microstructure, by using the Nb10 amorphous/ 
nanocrystalline BFM ribbon, high shear strength up to ~236 MPa was achieved for the TiAl alloy joint brazed at the relatively-low brazing temperature.
During compressive shear tests, the stress would concentrate in the (Ti, Zr)2(Cu, Ni) phase due to its high modulus, resulting in the initiation of cracks.

the interphase boundary between B2 and O-Ti2AlNb provided a pathway for dislocation transmission [40], which could accommodate the strain and relieve the stress concentration at the B2/O interphase boundary, thereby inhibiting crack initiation and propagation.

the stress would concentrate in the (Ti, Zr)2(Cu, Ni) phase due to its high modulus, resulting in the initiation of cracks.

the interphase boundary between B2 and O-Ti2AlNb provided a pathway for dislocation transmission [40], which could accommodate the strain and relieve the stress concentration at the B2/O interphase boundary, thereby inhibiting crack initiation and propagation.

The superior strength (~236 MPa) of the joint brazed with the Ti45Zr25Cu10Ni10Nb10 BFM at 1223 K for 30 min was primarily attributed to the formation of B2 + O-Ti2AlNb phases and the reduction of the brittle (Ti, Zr)2(Cu, Ni) phase at the braze zone center.
